clue.text: Having attempted a tackle, has got wiped out

definitions.meaning: to have gone for something is to have attempted it, and a burton is a kind of hoisting tackle used on ships
RAF slang from the Second World War for having been killed, or more loosely for being ruined or destroyed

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is read literally: 'gone for' means attempted, and a burton is a ship's hoisting tackle. The second is the British idiom for being killed or wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a literal attempt at a piece of ship's tackle, and the British slang idiom for being killed or written off.

clue.text: Receiving a tracheotomy, you will be reprimanded

definitions.meaning: a tracheotomy is a surgical cut into the windpipe, so the patient literally takes a blade in the throat
the idiom means to be severely scolded or punished

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being punished or scolded, read literally as an operation on the throat for the first sense.

clue.text: Figure twelve worn by horse

indicators.note: the time word is worn, like clothing, by the animal, so it wraps around it

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday is noon
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A rider's horse carries a number twelve cloth, as in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' means the time word wraps round the animal like a garment, though the surface suggests a racehorse carrying a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometric figure, so the shape is defined by its broad class.

clue.text: Fast boats

definitions.meaning: swift or quick on the feet, a literary adjective
a group of ships or boats sailing together, as in a navy

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for swift and a noun for a body of ships under one command.

clue.text: Recreate 'means of controlling ' opening

parts.note: a rein is the strap used to control a horse, hence any means of control
a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out

explanation.surface: Someone remakes a device for controlling an opening, like a valve.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvent is to make something again or anew, a direct synonym of recreate.

clue.text: Hang over game

definitions.meaning: to overhang or project, as beetling brows or cliffs do
a British party dice game in which players draw an insect part by part

explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is a British dice game where you draw a bug piece by piece, played at 'beetle drives'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means jut out or overhang, and as a noun it is a children's dice-and-drawing game.

clue.text: Direct one to work out what's obscure

indicators.note: the letters are set to work and come out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An instruction to send someone off to solve a puzzling problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work out' rearranges the nine letters of DIRECT ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is little known or abstruse, a close synonym of obscure.

clue.text: Rich having no let-up at work

indicators.note: the letters are busy at work, being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of the phrase without its hyphen

explanation.surface: A wealthy person who never takes a break from the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges the letters of NO LET-UP; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy or lavishly rich, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: The French upset familiar Prussian king and Saxon one

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads upwards

parts.note: la is a French word for the
Frederick the Great of Prussia, with his first name shortened to the familiar Fred

explanation.surface: A French tumble involving one Prussian monarch and a Saxon counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LA into AL. Frederick the Great ruled Prussia in the 1700s; Alfred the Great was a ninth-century king of Wessex, the West Saxons.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred was king of the West Saxons, so he is a Saxon king, the 'one' standing for the king already mentioned.

clue.text: Orange, brown, and green I mixed

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up, giving a new order

explanation.surface: A list of colours on a painter's palette being blended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange' looks like one more colour in the list, but it is the fruit being defined; 'mixed' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a kind of small orange citrus fruit, so the fruit is an example of oranges.

clue.text: Ill-bred person couldn't at first give a toss

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: to hurl is to throw, or toss, something

explanation.surface: A boorish person who simply couldn't care less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give a toss' looks like the British idiom for caring, but here it means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is a rude, boorish or mean-spirited person, which matches someone badly brought up.

clue.text: Firm hampered by lack of money

definitions.meaning: fixed securely or taut, as a firm knot
short of cash, as when money is ...

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means taut or secure, and also, of money, scarce or hard to come by.

clue.text: Offer one's services in adaptation of novel — true?

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks a novel for the screen, so its letters are reworked here

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a film version of a book is faithful, and offering to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in adaptation of' rearranges NOVEL and TRUE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer is to offer help freely, the verb sense matching the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Game bird returned to new home

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the bird's name is sent back, reading in reverse

parts.note: a snipe is a wading bird with a long bill

explanation.surface: A game bird flies back to its new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SNIPE into EPINS, which is added to N and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is a bowling game in which nine skittles are knocked down.

clue.text: Paper's head journalist' at centre of current exemplary court case

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the journalist goes into the middle of the following word

parts.note: recent means current or of the present time
ED is short for editor, a newspaper journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editor in chief is caught up in a landmark legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper's head' gives P; 'at centre of' places the editor in the middle of the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is an earlier legal decision that serves as an example for later cases.

clue.text: Fruit-rejected by lad' with exceptional talent

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the fruit is read in reverse

parts.note: a fig is a soft sweet fruit
Ted is a common boy's name, a crossword stock lad

explanation.surface: A boy who turns down fruit despite being highly talented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns FIG into GIF, followed by TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted describes someone with natural exceptional ability.

clue.text: This place, with others around, is heavenly

indicators.note: the others stand around this place, enclosing it

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others
here means this place

explanation.surface: A spot where others gather around seems heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the Latin abbreviation enclosing the place word; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and light, as if of the heavens, so it is a synonym of heavenly.

clue.text: What brings grist to the mill? Cricket, perhaps

definitions.text: What brings grist to the mill?
definitions.meaning: a funnel-shaped container that feeds grain into a mill
a cricket is an example of a jumping insect, as is a grasshopper

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the insect here, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the funnel feeding grain to millstones, the other any jumping insect such as a cricket.

clue.text: Take lead going round different plant

indicators.note: the metal symbol goes round the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
other means different

explanation.surface: Take the lead, go round a different plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' signals the chemical symbol enclosing the other word; 'Take' is only a link, though it looks like a recipe's R.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is a plant whose leaves are cooked or used to flavour food.

clue.text: Fully extended, eventually

definitions.meaning: stretched out to full length, as lying at full stretch

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at full length when stretched out, and also after a long delay or finally.

clue.text: Dazzling girl's outside with a token of affection

indicators.note: only the outer letters of the word are taken

parts.note: a ring is given as a token of love

explanation.surface: A girl's display of a love token is dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes G and L, the first and last letters of girl; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaring light is harsh and dazzling, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Mountain centre with service provided

parts.note: Mass is a church service
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A mountain retreat that offers church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact central mass of mountains, so it is the heart of a mountain range.

clue.text: Cathedral that's bizarre 'and remote

indicators.note: bizarre means odd, so the letters take an odd new order

explanation.surface: A strange and isolated cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' rearranges AND REMOTE; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre Dame in Paris is a famous cathedral, an example of the class.

clue.text: Some unceremonious language

indicators.note: some of the words, so the letters are found within them

explanation.surface: Informal speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'unceremonious' and the start of 'language', and the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, unceremonious language, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Plane sheltering fifty from the sun

indicators.note: the glide word shelters the numeral inside itself

parts.note: to plane is to glide or soar through the air
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An aircraft sheltering fifty people from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft but is the verb meaning glide. 'sheltering' puts L inside SOAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means coming from or relating to the sun.

clue.text: Man's spoken of busy junction

indicators.note: spoken of signals the word is said aloud

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A man is talked about at a busy junction.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE is a Cheshire town famous as a major railway junction; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The English town is famed as one of Britain's busiest railway junctions, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Bombardment finally. creates, inferno.

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of the following word

parts.note: hellfire is the fire of hell, an inferno

explanation.surface: A bombardment that ends by creating an inferno.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellfire is artillery fire, the shells of a bombardment.

clue.text: I had to succumb when embraced by-a lively; attractive woman

indicators.note: the first part is held inside the second, as if hugged

parts.note: bright means lively
to fall is to succumb or give in

explanation.surface: Someone had to give in when hugged by a lively, attractive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' signals the container; 'had' and 'when' are links. The phrase is British slang for an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang phrase is used for an attractive or desirable woman.
